headline: Tempus AI, a precision-medicine company, has expanded its work with Moderna and Merck to support a personalised cancer vaccine that is built for each patient.
score_reason: Company announcement without terms, timeline or results; relevant to personalised cancer care but still prospective.
importance_line: Cancer patients who may one day get a personalised vaccine, and the labs that would sequence their tumours, are affected, but the announcement gives no terms or timeline and speaks only of 'potential' commercialisation.
summary: Tempus AI says, in an announcement relayed by Oncodaily, that it has expanded its collaboration with Moderna and Merck to support the potential commercialisation of intismeran autogene, an individualised neoantigen therapy, meaning a treatment made for one patient from the mutations in their own tumour. Tempus will supply gene sequencing and sample-collection services; the wording 'potential commercialisation' shows the therapy is not yet on sale.
notes: Short article: Tempus's own statement, shared by CEO Eric Lefkofsky. The 'mutations in their own tumour' gloss is a standard definition of a neoantigen, not stated in the article; the article says only 'individualized neoantigen therapy' and 'personalized cancer vaccines'.
